CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right upper arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
39-year-old female presents with severe right upper arm pain following a volleyball injury sustained approximately 18 hours ago. Patient reports she was spiking the ball when an opponent kicked her legs out from under her, causing her to fall and land directly on her right shoulder. Pain is rated 9/10 in severity. Patient has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours with minimal relief. No ice has been applied to the injury. X-ray imaging reveals a proximal humerus fracture.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness or tingling in right arm. No other systemic complaints noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones. Lumbar fusion approximately 6 years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Pepcid (for gallstones). Ibuprofen every 6 hours.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in recreational volleyball.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient in acute pain. Right shoulder with swelling and erythema present. Tenderness noted over right shoulder. Able to straighten elbow with limited shoulder movement. Normal strength and range of motion in elbow and wrist. Normal pulses in right arm. Neurological exam intact with no numbness or tingling. Remainder of physical exam normal.

RESULTS
X-ray right arm: Proximal humerus fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture, right shoulder, secondary to sports injury. Plan: Immobilize with long arm cast and sling. Prescribe Lortab 5 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain (quantity 20). Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess fracture alignment. If bones have not realigned appropriately, will discuss surgical intervention at that time. Patient to be fitted with cast by technician prior to discharge.
